migrations.description: Core operational tables for M0/M1 with encryption CHECKs: users, keys, consents, birth/chart (birth_enc required), context signals (value pairing), content releases, readings (published ciphertext), connectors, jobs, audit, export/delete. Idempotency keys are scoped per user; user_keys is keyed by (user_id, key_version) so a destroyed key does not block re-keying and DEK rotation is possible; users.crypto_subject + id shape CHECKs; sessions table.

M3 daily reading pipeline. daily_readings gains a revision identity and loses the release-scoped uniqueness key (which permitted two published readings for one user-day whenever a release activated mid-day); jobs gains the DEK-encrypted immutable generation command, a durable outbox column, and a claim lease; reading_sources is rebuilt with constrained user ownership and a single encrypted evidence blob; cycle_passes adds the ordered pass list that makes the `reconsidering` phase reachable; users gains timezone and locale provenance plus a change log; assertion_probe provides a trigger-free conditional abort used both here and by the runtime publication guard.

M5 constrained-model reading publisher. daily_readings.release_version becomes nullable and is required exactly for deterministic rows, because a v5 reading has no editorial release behind it; status gains `invalidated`, the only state that removes a published artifact from Today before a successor exists, with invalidated_at required exactly then; the two reading_key grammars are held disjoint by namespace under the retained global UNIQUE (reading_key). reading_provider_daily_usage bounds provider spend by UTC date and is deliberately not keyed by user. Five partial indexes make the bounded scheduler and repair sweeps indexed rather than scanning: users next-due and unseeded cursors, failed readings below the command-generation ceiling, invalidated readings awaiting repair, and failed jobs by result class.

M6 privacy lifecycle and USR-06 check-ins. Rebuilds user_keys so only deletion-erased rows may lose wrapped DEK bytes; extends export/deletion requests with opaque job, receipt, envelope, checkpoint, timestamp, and safe error state; adds privacy-specific bounded outbox and lease indexes; and gives context signals deterministic source revisions, one-current-row semantics, non-unique evidence hashes, and bounded retention.

M4 Your Pattern and Time Travel. Adds deterministic natal-feature completion receipts, immutable bounded cycle-scan receipts, the per-user UTC-day outbound-scan ledger, and USR-09 revision/current-row uniqueness. Life-event values remain in encrypted context_signals and the three new tables are non-portable derived or operational state.

USR-05 sensitive-topic exclusions. One current encrypted context_signals row per owner, with uniqueness on (user_id, source_id) for the current row and on (user_id, source_id, source_revision) for the revision chain. No new encrypted column: values stay in context_signals.value_enc. USR-12 reading feedback uses the existing reading_feedback table and is not part of this migration.

M7 AI-generated Your Pattern. Rebuilds consents to admit pattern_generation without changing existing rows, carrying the two inbound consent references across the rebuild under live FK enforcement rather than switching foreign keys off. Adds per-fingerprint generation claims, Pattern-domain jobs, encrypted reader documents (body under a random document key; wrapped key under the user DEK), per-generation artifact keys, R2 artifact inventory, administrator access events, ontology release/pointer/evaluation/recall tables, and Pattern provider-budget ledgers.

M7 disaster-recovery replay ledger. Creates pattern_erasure_replay_events as the live D1 receipt for signed non-content lifecycle records (deletion, chart-correction erasure, withdrawal, claim consumption, account deletion, ontology recall). Not user-owned: no user_id column and no FK to users. A create-only R2 object is written first and is the restore authority; signing_key_id and replica_put_at are therefore non-null on every D1 receipt, and ontology recall requires a version tombstone. Not a crypto break and adds no encrypted column. The adapter's correction-document CHECK rebuild takes 0009; per-stage-class usage and any provenance-origin convenience column take 0010 or later.

M7 Pattern writer correction artifact. Forward-only rebuild of pattern_generation_artifacts under live foreign-key enforcement, preserving every existing inventory row and both indexes while widening only the artifact_class CHECK with correction_document. 0007 remains immutable; no encrypted column, schema-version change, or crypto-version change.

M7 provider-ledger stage attribution. Adds non-negative default-zero planner, writer, and verifier counters beside pattern_provider_daily_usage.used_calls, plus generator, evaluator, and regression counters beside pattern_ontology_provider_daily_usage.used_calls. Each used_calls column remains the shared total and ceiling quantity. Forward-only; no encrypted column or user identity.

M7 automated ontology pipeline terminal evidence handoff. Ordered after the reserved adapter migrations 0009 and 0010, without changing its SQL bytes. Adds one non-user-owned receipt whose committed identity is SQL-immutable and pins a succeeded run to a canonical R2 corpus manifest, corpus capability, bundle hash, a closed authenticated-encryption artifact envelope plus envelope/ciphertext hashes, independent evaluator result, activation scope, and signing key id. Public scope is constrained to licensed-excerpt/public-capable evidence. It deliberately leaves the future full Task 2 corpus/run/artifact table names free; those control-plane tables can later write this terminal receipt without a rebuild. Regression evidence is intentionally absent from this authorization row.

M7 automated ontology pipeline durable control plane. Additive and non-user-owned: immutable verified corpus inventory, frozen idempotent run commands with the closed stage machine, generation/cursor/attempt state, CAS lease and durable dispatch outbox, closed failures, evidence hashes and exact seven-day failed-artifact expiry, plus attempt-scoped create-only encrypted R2 artifact inventory. Partial indexes cover undispatched work, expired leases, and expired artifacts. D1 stores only pointers, pins, state, counts, and hashes; 0011 remains byte-identical and is populated separately at terminal success.

Durable external Codex CLI provider work exchange. Additive: immutable Pattern/ontology pass coordinates, frozen pins, bounded CAS leases, closed safe failures, and create-only encrypted R2 request/response inventory. ChatGPT credentials and provider plaintext remain absent from D1 and the Worker; Pattern-owned rows carry user_id only for erasure.

Lease-fenced Codex response upload inventory. Additive and content-free: records the hashed lease and unique encrypted R2 object key before upload, so reclaimed leases cannot conflict and stale objects remain discoverable by maintenance and account deletion.

Forward-only fail-closed regression evidence hardening for machine ontology activation. Adds an all-or-none nullable tuple pinning the canonical passed regression report and its exact create-only generic artifact coordinate, object key, envelope hash, and ciphertext hash. Existing committed receipts remain all-NULL and immutable and therefore cannot authorize machine activation; committed receipts cannot be deleted; no evidence is invented or backfilled.

M8 synchronous birth-calculation operational guards. Additive owner-scoped tables record exact UTC-day spend reservations, the winning hashed invocation claim, and monotonic profile-version allocation. The reservation ledger permits committed denial without a profile or job row and supports free same-coordinate replay. No encrypted column or content is added.

Admit the Daily `reading`/`publisher` coordinate on the Codex provider control plane. SQLite cannot alter a CHECK, so `codex_provider_jobs` is rebuilt forward-only with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` and `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = ON`: every response-upload child row is staged into a table with no foreign key of its own, the inbound foreign-key inventory is asserted, every parent column is copied explicitly and counted, the child and parent are dropped in dependency order so no ON DELETE CASCADE ever fires, the widened parent is renamed into place, and the child and all four indexes (idx_codex_provider_jobs_claimable, _owner, _user, and idx_codex_provider_response_uploads_created) are recreated with their 0013/0014 definitions before the staged rows are restored and counted. Only three relationship CHECKs widen: pipeline gains 'reading', pass gains 'publisher', and the pipeline/pass pair is a single closed relationship so reading admits only publisher, pattern keeps planner|writer|verifier, and ontology keeps its five passes; user ownership becomes pattern|reading NOT NULL and ontology NULL. Every lifecycle, envelope, lease, nonce, hash, safe-failure, uniqueness, and timestamp constraint is the 0013 text unchanged.

notes: M0 pre-production: 0001 is edited in place for encryption hardening. Do not apply an older 0001 against a live DB without a rewrite migration.

2026-08-01: 0001 edited in place for per-user idempotency scoping (uq_jobs_scope_key over COALESCE(user_id,''), plus UNIQUE(user_id, idempotency_key) on export_requests and deletion_requests), user_keys PRIMARY KEY (user_id, key_version) with a partial unique index on live keys, and KEK derivation v2. Local databases must be recreated: npm run db:local -w @patternlike/api. Rows written under KEK derivation v1 (bare SHA-256) are not readable under v2 (HKDF-SHA256); ensureUserKey rejects them with kek_version_unsupported rather than returning garbage.

2026-08-01: 0001 edited in place to add users.crypto_subject (the immutable AEAD/DEK subject, separate from the mutable users.id label), CHECK constraints on both id shapes, and the sessions table. AEAD_VERSION and KEK_DERIVATION_VERSION are both bumped in the same change because the AAD subject value changes from users.id to users.crypto_subject. Local databases must be DELETED and recreated, not just re-applied — every table statement is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so re-running 0001 over an existing database adds no column and still exits 0: rm -rf apps/api/.wrangler/state/v3/d1 && npm run db:local -w @patternlike/api. Pre-existing local rows are not readable.

2026-08-01: No schema change, but ciphertext written before this date is unreadable. AES-GCM additional authenticated data now binds every payload to (user_id, table.column, record id, key_version) and every wrapped DEK to (user_id, key_version). Payloads sealed without AAD fail authentication on read. Recreate local databases. Adding a new encrypted column requires adding it to ENCRYPTED_COLUMNS in apps/api/src/db/users.ts, or key rotation will leave its data under a destroyed key; rotateUserDek throws if it finds ciphertext in chart_snapshots.snapshot_enc, which is declared but not yet written.

2026-08-09: 0001 is IMMUTABLE from this point forward. 0002 is forward-only and is applied by `wrangler d1 migrations apply patternlike-ops`, not by `d1 execute --file`. It is NOT a crypto break: no AEAD_VERSION or KEK_DERIVATION_VERSION change, and existing ciphertext stays readable. It DOES add three encrypted columns — jobs.payload_enc, daily_readings.reading_enc, and reading_sources.evidence_enc — all three of which are registered in ENCRYPTED_COLUMNS in apps/api/src/db/users.ts. A new encrypted column that is not registered there is left under a destroyed key at the next rotation. 0002 REFUSES to run over non-empty daily_readings, reading_sources, or reading_feedback: those rows can only be re-shaped by an application layer holding the per-user DEK, so migration stops for an encrypted backfill rather than discarding them.

2026-08-09: APPLIED to production (patternlike-ops 1305a75d-0a8a-4a21-b201-d94fda0aaf93, ENAM) via `wrangler d1 migrations apply patternlike-ops --config apps/api/wrangler.toml --env production --remote`. Because 0001 had been applied with `d1 execute --file`, the database carried no d1_migrations table and wrangler replayed BOTH migrations: 0001 as a no-op (every statement is CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS, 38 commands) followed by 0002 (39 commands). d1_migrations now records both, so future applies are incremental. Pre-existing rows survived the jobs rebuild intact — users 2, user_keys 2, birth_profiles 2, jobs 2, identities 2, chart_snapshots 2, all unchanged, crypto_subject non-null on both users, and PRAGMA foreign_key_check returned empty. The reading tables were empty, so the assertion_probe abort never armed. Restore bookmark immediately prior to the apply: 0000001b-00000000-000050c2-0fc3bc90708a81d77df38b771f154055 (D1 time-travel retains ~30 days).

2026-08-10: 0003 is forward-only and applied by `wrangler d1 migrations apply patternlike-ops`. It is NOT a crypto break: no AEAD_VERSION or KEK_DERIVATION_VERSION change, no new encrypted column, and existing ciphertext stays readable. It DOES move context_signals.value_enc from UNWRITTEN_ENCRYPTED_COLUMNS to ENCRYPTED_COLUMNS in apps/api/src/db/users.ts — a list move made before the context compiler acquires its first writer, because a written column outside that list is left under a destroyed key at the next rotation. Like 0002, it REFUSES to run over non-empty daily_readings, reading_sources, or reading_feedback and aborts before either DROP. Production is expected to be empty for a structural reason rather than by luck: release_version was NOT NULL REFERENCES content_releases(version) and content_releases has no row, so no reading could ever have been written. The rollout runbook records the counts before applying rather than assuming them. users.next_due_at is NOT added here — 0001 already declared it and never wrote it, so 0003 only gives it its first two readers.

2026-08-14: 0007 is forward-only. It is NOT a crypto break. It adds pattern_documents.wrapped_document_key_enc and pattern_generation_artifact_keys.wrapped_key_enc to ENCRYPTED_COLUMNS, and lists pattern_documents.document_enc in NESTED_CONTENT_CIPHERTEXT_COLUMNS so DEK rotation rewraps the document key rather than re-encrypting the body. The frozen Pattern command reuses jobs.payload_enc. Consents are rebuilt only to widen the kind CHECK. The rebuild runs with foreign keys ENFORCED: D1 applies a migration file as one transaction and SQLite ignores PRAGMA foreign_keys inside a transaction, so DROP TABLE consents would raise FOREIGN KEY constraint failed against any context_source_permissions or context_signals row naming a consent, and PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys only moves the same failure to COMMIT because ALTER TABLE RENAME does not settle the deferred counter. Both consent_id columns are nullable, so 0007 stashes those references in a transaction-scoped table, nulls them for the length of the rebuild, and restores them once consents carries its original name, with an assertion_probe abort if the restored count does not match the stash. A third table gaining an FK to consents trips the probe at the top of the file.

2026-08-16: 0008 is specified and shipped as SQL. It is NOT applied to production in the same change that adds the file. It is NOT a crypto break and adds no encrypted column. A signed create-only R2 object is the durable write-ahead and restore authority; pattern_erasure_replay_events stores the live D1 receipt only after that put succeeds, with non-null signing_key_id and replica_put_at. Ontology-recall receipts require ontology_version so replay can clear the restored pointer and block re-ingestion. This R2-first order is intentionally privacy-conservative: an orphan intent may suppress content after replay, while the reverse order could lose an acknowledged erasure. No user_id column and no FK to users. The adapter's correction-document CHECK rebuild takes 0009; per-stage-class usage and any D1 provenance-origin convenience column take 0010 or later.

2026-08-20: 0010 is forward-only and is NOT applied by this change. It is NOT a crypto break and adds no encrypted column. Existing Pattern and ontology provider-ledger rows retain used_calls and gain non-negative default-zero stage-class counters. The shared ceilings remain enforced against used_calls; the new counters provide attribution only. The migration lands before rollout so both ledgers are still empty in deployed environments, while the migration setup also proves populated rows upgrade safely.

2026-08-20: 0011 is forward-only. It was authored while 0009/0010 were reserved; the ordered manifest now places both adapter migrations before its byte-identical SQL. It is NOT a crypto break and adds no encrypted column. Tasks 1-7 of the ontology pipeline are absent on this branch, so 0011 creates only the terminal evidence receipt Task 9 needs. The receipt overlaps the future Task 2 artifact table only by pinning that future row's object key, plaintext report hash, envelope hash, and ciphertext hash; the future source-corpus, pipeline-run, and pipeline-artifact tables retain their planned names and can populate this receipt on terminal success without a rebuild or FK to absent tables. Committed rows reject UPDATE, public scope requires licensed-excerpt/public-capable corpus evidence, and regression status/report/artifacts are deliberately not stored or read as authorization evidence.

2026-08-21: 0012 is forward-only and additive, ordered after the immutable 0011 terminal evidence receipt. It is NOT a crypto break and adds no D1 encrypted column: encrypted bodies remain create-only R2 objects while D1 holds only their closed class, object pointer, authenticated-envelope identity, hashes, size, and lifecycle timestamps. The corpus, run, and artifact rows are not user-owned and carry no user identifier or users foreign key. A clean-apply lane and a separately populated post-0011 lane verify exact order, live-row preservation, foreign-key integrity, assertion probes, closed constraints, and the three bounded maintenance indexes.

2026-08-24: 0013 is forward-only and additive. It is NOT a D1 crypto-version break and adds no plaintext or encrypted D1 content column: Codex request/response bodies live only in create-only AES-GCM R2 envelopes. D1 carries coordinates, pins, leases, safe failures, hashes, sizes, and R2 pointers. Pattern-owned rows carry user_id only so account erasure can delete their objects and control rows; ontology work remains non-user-owned.

2026-08-24: 0014 is forward-only and additive. It is NOT a crypto-version break and stores no provider content or plaintext lease: only job id, SHA-256 lease hash, create-only encrypted response object key, and timestamp. The pre-upload row is a durable cleanup/deletion inventory for attempts that lose terminal CAS after lease reclamation.

2026-08-24: 0015 is forward-only and additive. It preserves 0011 byte-for-byte and performs no backfill: pre-0015 committed receipts gain six NULL regression-evidence columns, remain immutable, cannot be deleted, and fail closed in the machine verifier. New machine receipts must populate the complete tuple with exact SHA-256 pins and the regressing/regression_report artifact coordinate; partial tuples are rejected on INSERT and UPDATE, committed rows reject DELETE, and non-NULL object keys are unique. It is not a crypto-version break and adds no encrypted D1 content.

2026-08-27: 0016 is forward-only and additive and is NOT applied by this change. It is NOT a crypto-version break: AEAD_VERSION and KEK_DERIVATION_VERSION are unchanged, existing ciphertext remains readable, and no encrypted D1 column is added. The three directly user-owned tables contain only bounded birth-calculation spend/idempotency state and a monotonic profile-version counter; they must be deleted with the account, remain non-portable, and land in D1 before any Worker code queries them.
